name: the defaults: frame 5 lost, 20 ms frames, 30 ms each way, 40 ms of buffer
why: The reference case. Frame n is sent at 20n, arrives at 20n + 30 and must play by 20n + 70. Fast retransmit: frame 8 is sent at 160 and arrives at 190, its duplicate ACK is back at 220, the resend arrives at 250, and 250 > 20n + 70 for n < 9, so frames 5 to 8 miss. Timeout: resend at 100 + 200 = 300, arrives at 330, and 330 > 20n + 70 for n < 13, so frames 5 to 12 miss. The chart and table are the same numbers per frame and have their own cases.

name: a 120 ms buffer absorbs fast retransmit entirely, and halves the timeout's damage
why: Frame n must now play by 20n + 150. Fast retransmit's repair still arrives at 250, which is exactly frame 5's deadline (100 + 30 + 120), and arriving at the deadline is on time, so nothing is missed. The timeout's repair arrives at 330, and 330 > 20n + 150 for n < 9, so frames 5 to 8 miss.

why: Resend at 100 + 1000 = 1100, arriving at 1130. 1130 > 20n + 70 for every n below 53, so every frame from 5 to the last, 20, misses: 16 frames, 320 ms. Fast retransmit is unchanged from the defaults because it never waits for the timer.

name: 60 ms frames: the 200 ms timer fires before the third duplicate ACK
why: Frame 8 is sent at 480, so its duplicate ACK is back at 480 + 60 = 540. The timer, started at 300, fires at 500 first, so both TCP rows resend at 500 and repair at 530. Frame n plays by 60n + 70, and 530 > 60n + 70 for n < 7.67, so frames 5 to 7 miss: 3 frames of 60 ms.

name: every frame of a short run, frame 2 lost of 6
why: The table is matched exactly, row by row. Frame n: sent 20n, arrives 20n + 30, plays by 20n + 70. Fast retransmit: frame 5 is sent at 100 and arrives at 130, its duplicate ACK is back at 160 (the timer would be 40 + 200 = 240), so the repair arrives at 190 and frames 2 to 6 are released then: 2 to 5 late, 6 exactly on its 190 deadline. Timeout: repair at 240 + 30 = 270, later than every deadline from frame 2 (110) to frame 6 (190).
